title: SSE nonce-based reconnect auth and semantic boundary preservation for function/tool outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers rely on long-lived SSE streams for low-latency responses, but transient network blips and client reconnects cause duplicated fragments, mixed function/tool call boundaries, and occasionally leak partial structured outputs. Existing resume tokens in other tickets assume in-order chunk ids and long-lived server session state, which complicates compatibility with lightweight clients and private deployments.

Goal: Implement a nonce-based reconnect handshake and semantic-boundary preservation layer that: (1) lets clients reconnect without requiring large server-side session state, (2) authenticates reconnects to avoid replay attacks, (3) preserves function/tool invocation boundaries and structured JSON outputs across reconnects, and (4) provides a compatibility shim for older clients that expect simple chunk ids.

Scope: server runtime changes (token/nonces, ephemeral session metadata), client-facing SSE header extension (X-Redwood-Reconnect-Nonce, X-Redwood-Last-Seq-Hash), controller/router routing logic (validate nonce, accept partial reassembly), and small SDK changes to expose reconnect headers and best-practice examples.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can reconnect and resume a stream using a server-signed nonce header without requiring long-lived server session objects
Function/tool call boundaries are preserved after reconnects: no mid-call JSON objects are emitted as separate semantic messages
Replay/replay-duplication surface is limited: the server detects repeated fragments using seq-hash and suppresses duplicates in the delivered event log
Legacy clients (no reconnect headers) continue to receive streams unchanged; compatibility shim logs warnings but does not change payload format
Unit + integration tests cover reconnect happy path, replay suppression, boundary healing, and failure modes with partial KV cache invalidation
Performance overhead on steady-state streaming < 2% p99 latency increase compared to baseline
technical_notes:
Design summary: generate a short-lived server-signed nonce per stream (TTL ~1m). Each emitted SSE event includes a monotonically increasing seq integer and a lightweight rolling SHA1 (seq-hash) of the last N events payloads for quick validation. On reconnect the client sends X-Redwood-Reconnect-Nonce and X-Redwood-Last-Seq-Hash. The router validates nonce signature and TTL. If seq-hash matches server's tail snapshot we trust the client position and resume; if it partially matches, we enter a healing mode where server replays a small window and merges fragments to preserve JSON/function-call boundaries. For unmatched or expired nonces fall back to a cold-restart (client receives a clear truncation marker event).

Boundary rules: function/tool calls are emitted as atomic semantic messages (SSE events may contain multiple chunks internally for transmission). Each semantic message is annotated with: boundary_id (UUID string), semantics: [response|tool-invocation|tool-result], and a preserved-json-checksum. During reconnect healing we never emit a tool-result that is a partial JSON; instead the server replays from the last known complete boundary_id and re-emits the whole semantic message.

Compatibility: we add an opt-in compatibility header X-Redwood-Compat-ChunkId for older clients; when present server will mirror legacy chunk-id behavior in addition to new headers. SDKs will default to modern headers.

Security: nonce is HMAC-SHA256(srv_key, stream_id || expiry || random). Nonces are single-use by default; we support a short reuse window (10s) to tolerate racey reconnects. We log suspicious reuse attempts and emit metric redwood.sse.reconnect.reject.reason. Requires a quick security review (see related link).
tasks: Spec PR: add header/nonce handshake + boundary semantics to streaming API spec
Runtime: implement nonce generation and validation in router layer
Runtime: add seq-hash tail snapshot store (bounded ring buffer per stream) and duplicate-suppression logic
Runtime: implement healing mode and semantic boundary replay
SDK: expose reconnect headers and example reconnection flow in JS and Python
Compatibility shim: opt-in legacy chunk-id echo mode
Tests: unit tests for HMAC nonce validation, seq-hash mismatch paths, boundary replay; integration tests with simulated flakey networks
Bench: performance run compare steady-state and reconnect latency p50/p95/p99
Docs: Console + API docs update, example rebuild for function-calling with reconnect
